A homeowner’s field guide

Repair or replace?
Start with the roof.

Age is one part of the picture. Condition, the extent of the problem,
and the details of the roof matter too.

What brought
you here?

Choose the situation closest to yours.

Questions before conclusions

Start by finding the source.

An isolated issue may be suitable for a repair when the surrounding roof is in sound condition. The visible leak does not always sit directly below the cause.

Worth asking

  • Where and when did you first notice the problem?
  • Is the surrounding roof in good condition?
  • What would the repair address, and what would it leave?
Talk through this situation

Questions before conclusions

Look at the roof as a whole.

Widespread deterioration or repeated issues make a broader assessment useful. Compare the condition of the covering and underlying layers before deciding.

Worth asking

  • How extensive is the deterioration?
  • Have previous repairs addressed the underlying issue?
  • What is included in a replacement proposal?
Talk through this situation

Questions before conclusions

A clearer picture comes first.

You do not need to choose repair or replacement before asking for help. Start with what you have noticed, what you know about the roof, and your plans for the home.

Worth asking

  • What is known about the roof’s age and history?
  • Are there interior signs of moisture?
  • What can an assessment establish?
